title: 26th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with 36 members present. Members put questions to the Minister of Education, mostly about delayed school building projects, classrooms, multipurpose halls and air-conditioning in their constituencies. Two Supreme Court judges' removal cases from the Judicial Service Commission were sent to the Judiciary Committee, a civil aviation bill had its first reading, and debate on the Housing Bill ended with its vote left for the voting time. Debate on a resolution about the Speaker's conduct also ended, and a committee report on a Sports Act amendment bill was under debate when this part ends. This part wraps up the committee-stage debate on the bill amending the Sports Act (Act 30/2015), then moves to the day's eleven votes. MPs accepted the Housing Bill and sent it to committee, rejected a resolution about how the chair runs proceedings, and adopted eight committee-report amendments to the Sports Act bill before passing the bill 70-0 with those amendments. The Speaker closed the sitting and set the next one for Tuesday 6 May 2025 at 9:00.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: As Minister of Education, answered questions on school projects, air-conditioning rollout, delayed contracts, multipurpose halls and the school-year calendar change.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Supported the Sports Act amendment report, saying the Sports Corporation model did not work and a sports fund replaces it.
Proposed eight amendments to the committee report, including registration and categorising of sports associations through the Commissioner of Sports.
Proposed that the Olympic and Paralympic committees send annual reports to the national sports council and the Commissioner by end of April.
Proposed replacing the term "club association" with "sports association" throughout the Act.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked about the academic-year change affecting resort staff and whether Addu schools are in the development plan.
On the Housing Bill, said the bill is needed but sincerity matters, and criticised how Addu City flats were handled.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: As Housing Bill sponsor, thanked supporters and urged the committee to finish quickly.
As committee rapporteur, presented the Sports Act amendment report, including a sports fund replacing the Sports Corporation.
Thanked the members who worked on the Sports Act bill in committee and the member who proposed the amendments.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked for an update on delayed school projects in Kulhudhuffushi, and about school space shortages.
Supported the Sports Act amendment committee report.
Seconded the member for Mahibadhoo's fifth amendment.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Asked about an independent survey or audit of the previous government's Naasthaa breakfast programme, and about students and a preschool in his area.
Seconded the member for Mahibadhoo's second amendment.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah

Supported the Sports Act amendment report.
Seconded the member for Mahibadhoo's first amendment.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad

Spoke on the Sports Act amendment report.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when work on Makunudhoo school's boundary wall, classrooms and multipurpose hall would start and begin serving students.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr

decisions: Case for removal of Supreme Court judge Dr. Azmiralda Zahir sent to the Judiciary Committee.
Case for removal of Supreme Court judge Mahaz Ali Zahir sent to the Judiciary Committee.
First reading of the Maldives Civil Aviation Bill was read.
Debate on the Housing Bill ended; acceptance of the bill is to be put to a vote at the voting time.
Debate on the resolution about the Speaker's conduct ended; the vote is left for the voting time.
Sitting paused 10:29 to 11:00, then resumed with the Sports Act amendment committee report.
The Housing Bill was accepted 71-0 and sent to the Gedhoruverikan committee for study.
A resolution on how the chair conducts proceedings, put forward by the member for South Galolhu, was not accepted (11 yes, 61 no).

Eight committee-report amendments to the Sports Act bill were adopted, including a registration and categorising role for the Commissioner of Sports and annual reports from the Olympic and Paralympic committees.
The bill amending the Sports Act (Act 30/2015) passed 70-0 with the Majlis amendments.
The Speaker read out the day's committee meeting times and set the next sitting for Tuesday 6 May 2025 at 9:00.
